paper_title: Constraints on Axion-like Particles from a Hard $X$-ray Observation of Betelgeuse
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 3 / Fig. 1
notes: First hard X-ray (NuSTAR, 50 ks) observation of Betelgeuse used to constrain ALP-photon coupling via Primakoff production in the stellar core and reconversion in the Galactic magnetic field. Not a dark-matter search, so no local DM density assumed. The 95% C.L. limit is quoted as a flat (mass-independent) bound below a mass cutoff, spanning g_agamma < (0.5-1.8)e-11 GeV^-1 for m_a < (5.5-3.5)e-11 eV depending on stellar model (t_cc) and transverse Galactic B-field (0.4-3.0 uG). I encoded the MOST CONSERVATIVE bound: g_agamma < 1.8e-11 GeV^-1 for m_a < 3.5e-11 eV (t_cc = 1.55e5 yr, B_T = 0.4 uG), extended down to 1e-14 eV per Fig. 1's plotted range. The most optimistic scenario (t_cc = 3.6 yr, B_T = 3.0 uG) gives g_agamma < 5.2e-12 GeV^-1 for m_a < 5.5e-11 eV.
